error.signature: AI tells someone in Pakistan they will automatically receive NDMA SMS flood/disaster warnings on any mobile network

verdict.summary: NDMA's geo-fenced monsoon flood SMS warning system (Disaster Early Warning System, DEW-3), launched under a partnership formalized in March 2025, is delivered only to Jazz subscribers - Pakistan's largest mobile operator, covering over 23 million subscribers in NDMA-identified flood-vulnerable areas. Users on other networks (Telenor, Zong, Ufone) are not covered by this specific SMS channel and must rely on the Pak NDMA Disaster Alert mobile app, NDMA's WhatsApp/UAN line, social media, or mainstream news for equivalent warnings.

dead_ends.action: Assume that being physically present in a flood-risk area of Pakistan is enough to automatically receive NDMA's monsoon SMS flood warnings, regardless of mobile carrier
dead_ends.why_fails: NDMA's geo-fenced DEW-3 monsoon SMS alert system was built through a March 2025 partnership specifically with Jazz; only Jazz's roughly 23 million subscribers in vulnerable zones receive these targeted SMS messages. It is not a telecom-wide cell-broadcast mandate covering Telenor, Zong, or Ufone users.
dead_ends.condition: Mobile subscriber on a network other than Jazz, in a flood-risk area
dead_ends.common_misconception: That Pakistan's flood SMS alerts work like an EU-style cell-broadcast public warning system available to every SIM regardless of carrier.

workarounds.action: Install the official Pak NDMA Disaster Alert mobile app (available on iOS and Android) for flood, earthquake, and other hazard alerts regardless of mobile carrier, and note NDMA's UAN (051-111-157-157) and WhatsApp (0300-0881641) contact lines for advisories
workarounds.how: The app delivers alerts over internet data rather than carrier SMS, so it works the same on Telenor, Zong, Ufone, or Jazz; combine it with mainstream news and NDMA's social media for redundancy.
workarounds.condition: Any mobile network subscriber wanting hazard alerts
